# Easy API ↔ Firestore Integration Guide

This doc captures the current Firestore-backed data model and the conventions for layering the Easy API on top of (or eventually replacing) it. It's the working brief for any session that touches Easy API integration — keep it up to date as endpoints are wired in.

> Code entry point: [lib/easy-api/server.ts](lib/easy-api/server.ts) — `EasyApiService` class + `easyApi` singleton.
> Auth: `x-easy-api-key` header sourced from `process.env.API_SECRET_KEY`. Base URL from `process.env.API_BASE_URL` (no `/v1` suffix — paths in domain modules must include their own version segment if needed).

---

## 1. Current Firestore data model

All collections live at the root of the default Firestore database. Type definitions are global ambient interfaces (no exports — referenced by name).

| Collection | Type | File | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `projects` | `Project` | [types/project.d.ts](types/project.d.ts) | Public read; admin-only writes. `id` is the Firestore doc ID. Dates stored as unix-ms `number`. |
| `transactions` | `Transaction` | [types/transaction.ts](types/transaction.ts) | Owner/admin read; admin-only update/delete. `type: 'investment' \| 'return'`. |
| `users` | `FirestoreUser` | [types/user.d.ts](types/user.d.ts) | Self-read/write only; `role: 'admin'` controls Firestore rules. `watchlist: string[]` of project IDs. |
| `documents` | `Document` | [types/document.ts](types/document.ts) | Authed read; admin-only write. |
| `waitlist` | `WaitlistEntry` | [types/waitlist.ts](types/waitlist.ts) | Doc ID is `${userId}_${projectId}`; admin read only, owner can join/leave. |

Security rules: [firestore.rules](firestore.rules). Storage rules: [storage.rules](storage.rules).

### Date convention
Every timestamp is `number` (ms since epoch) — `Date.now()` on write. The Easy API will likely use ISO 8601 strings; **transform at the boundary** (see §5).

### ID convention
Firestore-generated IDs come from `addDoc` or `doc(collection)`; the `id` field is denormalized onto the returned object only when read through the action layer. The Easy API likely returns IDs in the body — preserve this shape so consumer types stay stable.

---

## 2. Current Firestore action layout

- **Server-side** ([lib/firebase/server.ts](lib/firebase/server.ts)) — initializes a separate `'server'` named app, no auth context. Used by route handlers and server components.
  - [lib/firebase/server-actions.ts](lib/firebase/server-actions.ts) — projects (read all/by-id, create, update), `isUserAdmin`.
- **Client-side** ([lib/firebase/config.ts](lib/firebase/config.ts)) — default app, runs under user auth. Used by client components.
  - [lib/firebase/client-project-actions.ts](lib/firebase/client-project-actions.ts)
  - [lib/firebase/transaction-actions.ts](lib/firebase/transaction-actions.ts)
  - [lib/firebase/user-actions.ts](lib/firebase/user-actions.ts)
  - [lib/firebase/waitlist-actions.ts](lib/firebase/waitlist-actions.ts)
  - [lib/firebase/investment-actions.ts](lib/firebase/investment-actions.ts)
  - [lib/firebase/check-admin.ts](lib/firebase/check-admin.ts), [lib/firebase/auth.ts](lib/firebase/auth.ts), [lib/firebase/auth-context.tsx](lib/firebase/auth-context.tsx)

Each action file owns one collection and exposes `createX/getX/updateX/deleteX` style helpers that throw on error.

---

```
lib/easy-api/
  server.ts        ← base service, exports `easyApi` singleton + types
  types.ts         ← (when added) shared envelope types from Easy API spec
  projects.ts      ← domain methods: getProject, listProjects, createProject…
  transactions.ts  ← domain methods

  documents.ts
  waitlist.ts
```

```ts
// lib/easy-api/projects.ts
import { easyApi, type EasyApiResponse } from './server';

export type ProjectDto = Project & { id: string };

  easyApi.post<ProjectDto, ApiErrorBody>('/projects', { body });
```

```ts

```

Don't add zod schemas preemptively — wait for the actual Easy API response shape.

---

## 4. Envelope + error type (TBD)

The Easy API spec hasn't been shared yet. When it is, fill in these placeholders and add a typed wrapper to [lib/easy-api/server.ts](lib/easy-api/server.ts):


Existing example to mirror: [app/api/contact/route.ts](app/api/contact/route.ts) (zod parse → side effect → typed response).

```ts
// app/api/projects/[id]/route.ts

  if (!result.ok) {

  }
```

If the Easy API uses ISO strings and the existing UI expects unix-ms numbers, transform **inside the domain module** (single responsibility) before returning to the route handler:

```ts
const toUnixMs = (iso: string) => new Date(iso).getTime();

export const getProject = async (id: string) => {
  const res = await easyApi.get<RawProjectDto>(`/projects/${id}`);
  if (!res.ok) return res;
  return { ...res, data: { ...res.data, createdAt: toUnixMs(res.data.createdAt) /* … */ } };
```

---

## 6. Migration strategy

Pick one per collection — record the choice here as endpoints come online.

| Mode | When to use |
|---|---|
| **Read-through** | Route handler reads from Easy API only; writes still go to Firestore. Lowest risk first step. |

| **Dual-write** | Writes hit both Firestore and Easy API. Use only if Easy API is the source of truth target and Firestore is being decommissioned with a verification window. |
| **Full swap** | Both read and write go through Easy API. Firestore action file gets deleted. Final state. |

Status table — keep current:

| Collection | Mode | Endpoints wired | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `projects` | TBD | — | Public read on Firestore today; check whether Easy API requires auth for browse. |
| `transactions` | TBD | — | Sensitive — confirm Easy API auth model before swapping. |
| `users` | TBD | — | Firebase Auth still owns identity; Easy API likely stores app-level profile only. Clarify split. |
| `documents` | TBD | — | |
| `waitlist` | TBD | — | Composite key `${userId}_${projectId}` may not survive — check Easy API contract. |

---

## 7. Auth boundaries

- **Firebase Auth** stays as the user-identity layer (sign-in, ID tokens, `request.auth`). [lib/firebase/auth.ts](lib/firebase/auth.ts), [lib/firebase/auth-context.tsx](lib/firebase/auth-context.tsx).

---

- Don't reuse `lib/firebase/*-actions.ts` filenames for Easy API — keep the layers visibly distinct (`lib/easy-api/projects.ts`, not `lib/easy-api/project-actions.ts`).

---

## 9. Open questions to resolve before wiring endpoints

1. **Response envelope** — `{ data: T }` / `{ result: T }` / raw `T`?
2. **Error shape** — fields on a non-2xx body. Codes? Field-level details?
3. **Date format** — ISO 8601 strings vs unix-ms numbers vs seconds?
4. **ID format** — does Easy API generate IDs server-side, or expect client-supplied?
5. **Pagination** — cursor / offset / page-number? Needs deciding before `listProjects` etc.
6. **User identity propagation** — does Easy API need a user ID in headers/body, or is the secret key alone sufficient + multi-tenant per request?
7. **Versioning** — does Easy API have a version segment we need to bake into paths (since `API_BASE_URL` doesn't include one)?

Answer these inline above and remove the question once resolved.

Good news first: **payment-link is the right primitive for this flow** — same model as Stripe Checkout (we hand off, they collect, we listen for the result). Solid choice. Below is what's actually missing before that POST will succeed end-to-end.

## The flow — short answer

Yes, this works. Payment-link is hosted-checkout: you create the link server-side, redirect the user, Easy API handles the payment UI/PCI/3DS, then redirects back. **But the link itself only confirms the user *started* the flow** — to know an investment actually succeeded you need a **webhook** (not in the endpoint you sent). Without it, only the success-return URL signals payment, and that's unreliable (user closes the tab, network blip, etc.).

## Critical missing pieces

### 1. Easy API products + prices don't exist yet
The endpoint requires `products[].product_prices[].id` — that's a `price_xxx` ID **registered in Easy API**, not anything from your DB. So before you can call this endpoint at all, you need to:
- Create one or more Products + Prices in Easy API (probably via a separate endpoint or their dashboard — confirm).
- Decide on the model: **one Price per project** (variable amount, simplest), or **one Price per Perk tier** (fixed amounts, lets the tier drive the price).

My recommendation for an investment app: **one Price per project, `amount_type: VARIABLE`**, with `min_amount` and `max_amount` from `Financials.minInvestment` and remaining capacity. Tiers can still be selected client-side and passed through `tags` for record-keeping; perk-fulfillment isn't payment's problem.

### 2. Project type needs an Easy API price reference
[types/project.d.ts](types/project.d.ts) has no link to Easy API. Add to `Financials` (or top-level on `Project`):
```ts
easyApiProductId?: string;   // 'prod_xxx'
easyApiPriceId?: string;     // 'price_xxx' — the one referenced in product_prices
```
Backfill these when each project is registered with Easy API.

### 3. Transaction needs lifecycle + Easy API IDs
[types/transaction.ts](types/transaction.ts) is single-state (no `status`). Payment is multi-step (created → completed/failed/expired). Add:
```ts
status: 'pending' | 'succeeded' | 'failed' | 'expired' | 'canceled';
amountCents: number;          // Easy API speaks cents (integer)
currency: 'USD';              // confirm — currency is set on the Price, not the link
easyApiPaymentLinkId: string; // 'pl_xxx'
easyApiPaymentId?: string;    // populated on webhook success
```
This breaks existing investment-actions and any dashboard component reading `Transaction.amount`. Migration: dual-write `amount` (dollars) + `amountCents` for one release, or convert and bump everything at once. The latter is cleaner since you're pre-launch.

### 4. Money convention mismatch
Easy API uses **integer cents** (`min_amount`, `max_amount`, `amount_cents` in the response). Your model uses **dollars as `number`** everywhere (`Financials.minInvestment`, `Project.moneyRaised`, `Transaction.amount`). Convert at the Easy API boundary inside the domain module — don't leak cents into the rest of the app.

### 5. Date convention mismatch
Easy API: ISO 8601 strings (`"2026-02-06T12:00:00.000Z"`). Your model: unix-ms `number`. Same answer — convert at the boundary.

### 6. New env vars
Add to `.env.local`:
```
NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=https://benicapital.com    # for return URLs
EASY_API_WEBHOOK_SECRET=                       # for verifying webhook signatures
```
You don't have a base-URL env today; you need one to build the absolute return URLs the endpoint requires.

### 7. New API routes
- `POST /api/easy-api/payment-link` — creates the link. Verifies Firebase ID token, checks project status, validates amount against `minInvestment`, creates a **`status: 'pending'` Transaction in Firestore first**, then calls Easy API with `tags: { projectId, userId, transactionId }`, returns the URL.
- `POST /api/easy-api/webhook` — receives payment success/failure events. Verifies signature, looks up the pending transaction by `transactionId` from `tags` (idempotency-safe — never double-record), updates status, increments `Project.moneyRaised`. **This is the source of truth.**
- `GET /payment/success` and `GET /payment/canceled` — pure UX pages. Don't trust them for state changes; just show "we're confirming your payment" and let the webhook drive the data.

### 8. Required `terms_of_service_url`
Body schema requires `additional_details.terms_of_service_url`. Use [/terms-of-service](app/terms-of-service/) — that page already exists.

## End-to-end flow I'd build

```
1. User clicks "Invest $X" on project page (client)
2. Client → POST /api/easy-api/payment-link  { projectId, amount }
3. Route handler:
   - verifies Firebase ID token
   - loads project, checks status === 'fundraising', amount >= minInvestment
   - creates Firestore transaction { status: 'pending', amountCents, ... }
   - calls easyApi.post('/v1/api/payment-link/', { body: {
       amount_type: 'VARIABLE',
       min_amount: <project.minInvestment * 100>,
       max_amount: <project.amount * 100>,
       products: [{ product_prices: [{ id: project.easyApiPriceId, quantity: 1, adjustable: true }] }],
       allowed_payment_methods: ['PAYMENT_CARD', 'BANK_ACCOUNT'],
       payment_frequency: 'ONE_TIME',
       is_multiple_use: false,
       collect_buyer_details: 'email',
       tags: { projectId, userId, transactionId, type: 'investment' },
       additional_details: {
         terms_of_service_url: 'https://benicapital.com/terms-of-service',
         success_return_url: '<APP_URL>/payment/success?t=<transactionId>',
         unsuccessful_return_url: '<APP_URL>/payment/canceled?t=<transactionId>',
         expired_session_url: '<APP_URL>/payment/canceled?t=<transactionId>',
         send_receipt: true,
         expiration_in_minutes: 60,
       },
     } })
   - returns { url } from response.data.url
4. Client redirects to url
5. User pays on Easy API hosted page
6. Easy API webhook → /api/easy-api/webhook → verify signature → find pending transaction by tags.transactionId → mark succeeded → bump project.moneyRaised
7. User lands on /payment/success → page polls/listens for the Firestore transaction status
```

## Open questions to confirm with Easy API

These block real implementation:

1. **Product/Price creation** — is there a `POST /v1/api/products/` and `/v1/api/prices/` endpoint, or is it dashboard-only? You'll need to register every project's price programmatically if you want this to scale.
2. **Currency** — is it set on the Price (not the link)? The endpoint body doesn't take a currency field, but the response includes one. Confirm.
3. **Webhook delivery** — what's the events endpoint, payload shape, and signature header name? This is where most integration time will go.
4. **Idempotency key** — does Easy API support an `Idempotency-Key` header on this POST? If a user double-clicks, can we safely retry?
5. **`is_multiple_use` semantics** — for an investment, set to `false` so each click → one paid link → one transaction.
6. **Adjustable amount UX** — with `VARIABLE` + `adjustable: true`, can the user change the amount on the hosted page (bad — we already validated server-side), or is it locked once the link is created (good)?

## Suggested order

1. Confirm the six open questions above with Easy API docs / support.
2. Add `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` and `EASY_API_WEBHOOK_SECRET` env vars.
3. Update [types/project.d.ts](types/project.d.ts) (`easyApiPriceId`) and [types/transaction.ts](types/transaction.ts) (`status`, `amountCents`, `easyApiPaymentLinkId`).
4. Update Firestore rules — make the new fields readable/writable correctly (only server can write `status`, etc.).
5. Build [lib/easy-api/payments.ts](lib/easy-api/payments.ts) with `createPaymentLink(...)` typed against the schema you sent.
6. Build the two API routes (`payment-link`, `webhook`).
7. Wire dashboard "Invest" button.
8. Add `/payment/success` and `/payment/canceled` pages.

Good — that fixed-tier rule changes the design significantly, and for the better. The previous "one Price per project, VARIABLE amount" plan is now wrong; here's the simpler model.

## The pivot: 6 global prices, not per-project

Since all six tiers ($5k / $10k / $25k / $50k / $100k / $250k) apply to every project, we don't need to create per-project Prices in Easy API. Instead:

- **One-time bootstrap (per environment):** create **1 Product** ("Beni Investment") + **6 Product-Prices** (one per tier, `unit_amount` in cents, `recurring: false`). Store the 6 `price_xxx` IDs in env vars.
- **Per-project setup in Easy API: zero.** New projects need no Easy API call.
- **At invest time:** route handler maps the user-selected tier to the matching `price_xxx`, includes `tags: { projectId, userId, transactionId, tier }` on the payment-link, and Easy API's hosted page shows a fixed-amount checkout.

This removes `easyApiPriceId` from `Project` entirely (the prices are global, not project-scoped).

> **Alternative I considered and rejected for MVP:** one Product *per* project (with 6 prices each). Cleaner receipts ("Investment in *Cinderella's Castle*" vs generic "Beni Investment"), but couples project creation to Easy API and 7× the bootstrap surface. Worth revisiting post-launch if receipt clarity matters — `tags` + a custom email template is probably enough.

## What you actually need now

### A. New env vars (after bootstrap)
```
NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=https://benicapital.com
EASY_API_WEBHOOK_SECRET=                     # filled in after creating the webhook endpoint in their dashboard
EASY_API_PRICE_ID_5K=
EASY_API_PRICE_ID_10K=
EASY_API_PRICE_ID_25K=
EASY_API_PRICE_ID_50K=
EASY_API_PRICE_ID_100K=
EASY_API_PRICE_ID_250K=
EASY_API_PRODUCT_ID=                         # optional — only if we ever need to fetch/update the product
```

### B. Bootstrap script
A small, run-once `scripts/setup-easy-api-products.ts` that:
1. POSTs `/v1/api/products/` with `name: "Beni Investment"`, `description`, `active: true`, `image_url` (the Beni logo URL), `metadata: { app: "beni-capital" }`.
2. POSTs `/v1/api/product-prices/` six times, one per tier, with the returned `product_id`.
3. Prints all 7 IDs so you can paste them into `.env.local`.

Run once per environment (dev / staging / prod) → done forever.

### C. Tier constants
A single source of truth at e.g. `const/investment-tiers.ts`:
```ts
export const INVESTMENT_TIERS = [
  { dollars: 5000,   cents: 500_000,    envKey: 'EASY_API_PRICE_ID_5K'   },
  { dollars: 10000,  cents: 1_000_000,  envKey: 'EASY_API_PRICE_ID_10K'  },
  { dollars: 25000,  cents: 2_500_000,  envKey: 'EASY_API_PRICE_ID_25K'  },
  { dollars: 50000,  cents: 5_000_000,  envKey: 'EASY_API_PRICE_ID_50K'  },
  { dollars: 100000, cents: 10_000_000, envKey: 'EASY_API_PRICE_ID_100K' },
  { dollars: 250000, cents: 25_000_000, envKey: 'EASY_API_PRICE_ID_250K' },
] as const;
```
The investment buttons on the project page render from this array; the API route uses it to resolve `tier → priceId`.

### D. Type changes (smaller than before)
- [types/project.d.ts](types/project.d.ts) — **no Easy API fields needed**. (`Financials.minInvestment` becomes display-only — your real minimums are the tier values.)
- [types/transaction.ts](types/transaction.ts) — still needs the lifecycle fields:

  ```ts
  status: 'pending' | 'succeeded' | 'failed' | 'expired' | 'canceled';
  amountCents: number;
  currency: 'USD';
  tierDollars: 5000 | 10000 | 25000 | 50000 | 100000 | 250000;
  easyApiPaymentLinkId: string;
  easyApiPaymentId?: string;
  ```

### E. Edge case to decide: tier gating per project
`Financials.targetInvestment - moneyRaised` is each project's remaining capacity. If a project has only $30k left, do you:
- (a) Still show all 6 buttons and let users overshoot the goal? Permissive — the project becomes over-funded, which is often fine and can be a feature.
- (b) Hide tiers that exceed remaining capacity? Strict — only $5k, $10k, $25k visible in that example.
- (c) Hide tiers below the project's `minInvestment`? Some projects in your `Financials` use a higher floor.

My read of "every project, these 6 options" is **(a)** — keep it dead simple. Flag this in the doc as a product call.

### F. Webhook setup
From your screenshot: you'll register the endpoint in their dashboard. Subscribe to **only what we handle** (less noise, easier debugging):

| Event | What we do |
|---|---|
| `payment.created` | Optional log; the pending Transaction already exists from our route handler. |
| `payment.updated` | **Primary handler.** Reads new status, marks Transaction `succeeded`/`failed`/`canceled`/`expired`, increments `Project.moneyRaised` on success. |
| `refund.created`, `refund.updated` | Mark Transaction refunded; decrement `moneyRaised`. |
| `dispute.created`, `dispute.updated` | Flag for admin review; don't auto-decrement (let admin decide). |
